pages.title: Hold That Moment
pages.text: Start real photography; black-and-white film and paper carry the workflow toward your first prints.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.text: Sneak-use for attachments, insert film and enter the viewfinder. Controls include shutter, guides, spyglass lens, flash and timer; film labeling keeps rolls organized.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Insert a film roll into a camera via the sneak-use attachments UI, then enter the viewfinder. Camera can expose frames rather than merely taking screenshots.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: While in the viewfinder, use camera controls for shutter speed, composition guides and installed flash. Capture a film frame with chosen settings.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Sneak-use the Camera or right-click it in inventory, then choose film, flash, lens or filter. Configure attachments; the installed tooltip also documents quick swapping by item interaction.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Install a Spyglass lens and use the viewfinder scroll wheel. Change the camera's zoom range and framing.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Use a film roll to open its renaming flow. Organize exposed rolls without an anvil experience cost; the label survives developing.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Use the native frame-exposed criterion to describe a real photographed subject instead of checking camera possession. Installed adventure/exposure advancement proves the frame_exposed trigger; family_portrait demonstrates entity predicates.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Rename an Interplanar Projector to a supported image file path or URL, install it as a camera filter and expose a frame. Import the image subject to server configuration; the projector is consumed or breaks on failure.

pages.title: Related possibilities
pages.text: Load film, compose through the camera view, expose frames, develop the roll, then select and print a frame at the Lightroom. The tutorial corroborates this order and distinguishes black-and-white versus color supplies; it also demonstrates zoom, composition guides and camera attachments.
